card.title: 1er BCP
card.text: Draw a card when the enemy draws a RESISTANCE order.
card.flavorText: Created in 1840, the 1er Bataillon de Chasseurs à Pied (1er BCP) belonged to the French Army's 43rd Infantry division at the start of WWII. During the Battle of France, it fought in northern France at La Longueville and La Bassée, before falling back towards Dunkirk, from where it was evacuated during Operation Dynamo. It returned to France a few days later in an attempt to re-establish a front in Normandy, before being taken prisoner on the day of the armistice. Disbanded in November 1942, it was reformed a first time in September 1944 during the liberation of France, as part of the Swiss Groupe Mobile d'Alsace (GMA), with Alsatians who had refused forced conscription or deserted from the Wehrmacht, having taken refuge in Switzerland. It took part in the fighting to liberate southern Alsace, notably around Seppois-le-Bas where it repelled, alongside the 152e Régiment d’infanterie, a counter-attack by the Wehrmacht's 198th Infantry division on November 25th. In December, the Alsatians were released from their military obligations, but many members of the Swiss GMA enlisted in the new 31e BCP to continue the fight. The 1er BCP was reformed a second time on January 1st, 1945 and took part in the fighting in the Saint-Nazaire pocket, until the German capitulation.
